newsitem.title: USA: SEC bars Osborne from securities industry.
newsitem.headline: SEC bars Osborne from securities industry.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Tuesday Douglas Osborne, a California ostrich farmer, has been barred from doing business in the securities industry.

"The record establishes beyond a reasonable doubt that Mr. Osborne cannot be trusted, and that he has no regard for statutes and legal norms," wrote Chief Administrative Law Judge Brenda Murray in her August 18 decision and order.

The administrative law judge's decision comes three years after a federal judge ordered Osborne and his firm to pay more than $200,000 on the SEC's charges relating to the telemarketing and sale of shares in Consolidated Energy Systems Inc, a penny stock company his firm controlled.

The SEC in its civil suit alleged Osborne failed to tell investors that his firm controlled the company and that they were being charged excessive mark-ups ranging from 11 percent to 167 percent of his firm's costs.
In 1992, the Federal Trade Commission filed similar charges against Osborne, relating to his telemarketing activities.
Several states and the National Association of Securities Dealers have also penalized Osborne and his firm.
Osborne could not be reached for comment.
